title: distributed-sqlite-cache
tagline: An embedded edge cache running SQLite in memory with peer-to-peer replication over QUIC.
whatWentWrong: We initially used Raft for consensus across 15 edge nodes, but network jitter on mobile edge points caused leader election flapping every 3 minutes. We had to scrap our Raft implementation entirely in week 3 and switch to an eventual consistency CRDT model with vector clocks. It delayed the prototype by 10 days, but dropped CPU overhead by 70%.

children.text: Most modern SaaS backends pay an outrageous monthly fee for multi-region Redis clusters simply to cache small read-heavy user sessions and authorization tokens.

When users in Singapore hit a US-East server for session tokens, they incur an unavoidable 210ms roundtrip delay. Sticking Redis at the edge solved latency, but the replication costs were painful for a team of 4 engineers.

Instead of running a separate memory daemon, we embedded in-memory SQLite directly into each edge worker process. Each node maintains its own local b-tree cache and synchronizes mutation deltas over QUIC streams.
The result: p99 read latencies dropped from 145ms to 2.4ms, and our infrastructure bill went from $850/month to $34/month.
